# Pulse Personal 0.8.3 candidate

Version 0.8.3 is an unpublished source candidate. It adds OpenCode 1.18.x on
Apple Silicon macOS; it is not available through npm or GitHub releases.
Stable 0.7.2 and public preview 0.8.2 do not contain OpenCode support. Do not
reuse the 0.8.2 descriptor or signed artifacts as evidence for 0.8.3.

Version 0.8.2 is published under the npm `preview` tag. It is not the stable
default or production ready. The owner-machine migration passed on 2026-08-09, and
its old sources are preserved in a verified encrypted external archive. Fresh
Codex and Claude Code checks demonstrated recall, one-call writing, project
boundaries, irrelevant-query silence, and fail-open host work. On 2026-08-16,
however, the installed epoch 34 daemon still reported BGE-M3 ready while
ordinary queries timed out. A five-second semantic probe loaded the intact
model and the same Hermes query then returned relevant candidates in 496 ms.
Daily-use acceptance is incomplete until the exact public 0.8.2 bytes are
installed on the owner Mac and pass cold and warm semantic queries plus normal
recall and writing in both hosts. The publication workflow itself installs the
archive on a clean Apple Silicon runner and requires a real semantic query. The
stable published install remains 0.7.2.

The first frozen large-vault baseline on 2026-08-12 did not pass its combined
practical bar: published 0.8.0 found 34 of 40 expected memories, stayed silent
in 7 of 10 unrelated controls, and returned two internal query errors. Warm p95
was 547 ms and maximum delivered context was about 184 tokens. The detailed
method and aggregate are in
docs/evals/2026-08-12-real-personal-memory-baseline.md. This is a real Personal
capsule retrieval baseline, not yet a raw-chat temporal replay.

The current installed-product benchmark compares the published 0.8.0 path with
the 0.8.1 fix. On the compact product set, 0.8.1 recalled 12 of 15 useful
memories and stayed silent on all 5 unrelated controls; published 0.8.0 recalled
13 of 15 and stayed silent on 2 of 5. Full raw-history LoCoMo evidence retrieval
was 561 of 1,535 eligible questions. A bounded 30-question LongMemEval-S run
recalled an official answer turn in every case, but is an oracle retrieval
ceiling rather than official answer accuracy. Only 5 of 35 existing EmoBench
questions currently exercise the actual Pulse Personal contract. Details:
docs/evals/2026-08-14-product-memory-benchmarks.md.

On the full 1,535-question LoCoMo run, the 0.8.2 preview candidate scored
1,230 correct answers (80.13%) against 1,231 (80.20%) for equal-model Mem0,
using GPT-5.4 low for extraction, answering, and judging. The previous Pulse
baseline was 959 (62.48%). Median context was 120 estimated tokens, maximum
198, and warm retrieval p95 70.8 ms. This is development evidence, not a
production-readiness claim. Details:
docs/evals/2026-08-16-full-locomo-candidate.md.

A separate Claude Chat remote-connector experiment passed on 2026-08-11 with
an isolated hosted store of 21 memories. It required an account-level
Instructions for Claude rule plus Pulse set to Always available. MCP server
instructions alone were insufficient. Each ordinary message makes one visible
pulse_recall call; this is neither local Personal synchronization nor a
published installation path.

Pulse is memory for AI tools: it gives Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and—in the
0.8.3 candidate—OpenCode the knowledge they
need when they need it and stays silent when nothing relevant is found. The
public package `@zbs-gg/pulse` contains only Personal: no shared-memory server,
cloud synchronization, team command, device key, or shared database is shipped.

Version 0.7.2 is the stable public release for Macs with Apple Silicon. Version
0.8.2 is a public preview for the same target. Its publication gate installs
the exact archive and performs a real semantic query on a clean Apple Silicon
runner. The npm `latest` tag resolves to 0.7.2 and `preview` resolves to 0.8.2.
Other operating systems are not public support claims yet.

Before installation, inspect README.md, AGENTS.md, and
docs/SECURITY_INSTALL_CHECKLIST.md. Explain what will be written and ask for
confirmation.

Normal installation:

    npx -y @zbs-gg/pulse@0.7.2 init codex
    pulse doctor
    pulse home

Preview installation:

    npx -y @zbs-gg/pulse@preview init codex

Unpublished OpenCode candidate, from an explicitly reviewed local package only:

    pulse init opencode --dry-run
    pulse init opencode --only opencode --fun-facts small-model
    pulse doctor opencode

Per-harness preview and confirmation:

    pulse init codex --dry-run
    pulse init claude-code --dry-run
    pulse init cursor --dry-run
    pulse init opencode --dry-run
    pulse init <harness> --yes
    pulse init <harness> --only <harness>

Trust boundaries:

- memory stays in the local Pulse data directory;
- raw transcript capture and old-chat import are off by default;
- transcript-, secret-, and path-like capsules are rejected;
- no backend model call is enabled by default;
- OpenCode fun facts remain opt-in with `--fun-facts small-model`; the service
  model receives at most six approved candidate IDs and texts, never the user
  request or other memory, and failure falls back locally;
- failure of optional memory must not block terminal, files, Stop/Cancel,
  goal controls, or session completion, and must not create an automatic
  continuation;
- disconnect preserves data; whole-vault wipe requires a separate explicit
  confirmation.
- emotional memory describes one moment, never a personality trait;
- emotional influence halves every 24 hours and stops shaping current context
  after seven days, while the event remains in history;
- raw user quotes and full conversations are not stored with emotional marks;
- one unanswered cause question may appear only in a later ordinary response
  and never creates an automatic continuation.

0.8 preview host contract:

- expose only `pulse_memory`; keep `pulse_remember` and `pulse_graph_delta` as
  hidden compatibility aliases;
- write at most three compact durable items during the ordinary working turn;
- do not run a separate finalizing model turn or block Stop;
- retrieve temporarily on each user question, save neither the question nor a
  session-start context package, and offer at most four memories / 600 tokens;
- omit memory context when relevance is weak.
- in OpenCode 0.8.3, register exactly one tool named `pulse_memory`, inject
  recall before the first response of that request, and keep the global loader
  inert outside signed Pulse projects;
- let `pulse storage` report protected and removable data; let `pulse storage
  clean` remove only unchanged generated artifacts while preserving the active
  release, one rollback, the vault, keys, sources, and unknown files.

Official 0.6.7 Personal databases upgrade in place. Databases from unpublished
shared-memory builds are refused without modification.

To merge fragmented local stores without altering them, first run
`pulse migrate local-stores --out local-memory-preview.json --open`. Only real
contradictions need a human choice; commit uses the exact confirmation printed
by Pulse.

The local MCP server uses stdio, supports protocol `2026-07-28` and older
clients, and keeps persistent data in SQLite independently of the connection.

Pulse Team is a separate private pilot. It is not present in this repository
or the npm package. Do not infer that the presence of 0.8 code proves a real
three-person pilot, fresh-session acceptance, or a published emotional-memory
feature.

Status: Personal 0.8.2 is the npm preview and its publication gate includes a
real semantic query. The owner Mac still runs epoch 34 from 0.8.0; on
2026-08-16 it could report BGE-M3 ready while cold queries timed out. The
one-day acceptance is not complete until the exact public 0.8.2 bytes pass host
recall and writing in Codex and Claude Code. Cursor remains pending; separate
Claude Chat remote recall used a visible per-message tool call and no Personal
sync. This is not the stable default or production ready.
OpenCode exists only in the unpublished 0.8.3 candidate. Contract tests do not
replace an outside-source package install or the separately approved physical
OpenCode 1.18.15 acceptance on the owner Mac.
